Access key rotation

Replace the AWS access key you use to upload Diamond 2 XML files. Your current key is used to mint its replacement and is then retired. Nothing you enter here leaves your browser except to AWS.

1

Current key

Enter the access key you use today. It needs permission to manage its own keys, which is how your key was issued.

2

Key slots

AWS allows two access keys per user. Rotation uses the spare slot, so if both are full you must retire one before creating a replacement.

3

Save the new credentials

AWS returns the secret once and never again. Save it into your upload configuration or secret store before you go on.

This secret disappears when you close this tab

4

Verify the new key

New keys take a few seconds to become usable across AWS. This calls AWS with the new credentials until they answer.

5

Retire the old key

Deactivate first. If an upload fails you can switch the old key back on. Delete only once you have seen a successful upload on the new key.

What this page does, and does not, do

Every request goes directly from your browser to https://iam.amazonaws.com, signed with AWS Signature Version 4 using the Web Crypto API. There is no back end, no analytics, no external script, stylesheet or font. The Content Security Policy on this page permits network access to the AWS IAM endpoint and nowhere else, so you can verify that claim in your browser's network tab.

When this page is opened from the Diamond 2 uploader's own site, it reads the access key saved in the uploader's settings (this browser's local storage) so you do not have to re-enter it, and after the replacement key is verified it saves the new key back to the same place, so the uploader switches to the new key automatically. It reads and writes only the access key ID and secret — nothing else — and only in this browser.

Run from a saved copy of this file, or from anywhere other than the uploader's site, it stores nothing at all: credentials are held in page memory only and closing the tab discards everything.

The page calls four IAM actions: ListAccessKeys, CreateAccessKey, UpdateAccessKey and DeleteAccessKey. It never reads or writes anything in your upload bucket.

You can save this file and run it from your own machine or intranet rather than loading it from us. It has no dependencies and works from a file:// URL.
